summary: Backend-only regression for iteration_63 covering the Google session / Emergent consent-screen fix (frontend-side fix was in AuthContext.tsx, no backend changes this session). 16/16 pytest tests PASS (100%). Covered: (1) GET /api/auth/me — valid JWT → 200 with correct user_id/email, invalid token → 401, missing header → 401, malformed header → 401. (2) POST /api/auth/logout — no token → 200 ok; with a real session_token row in user_sessions → row is deleted from DB and subsequent /auth/me returns 401. (3) POST /api/auth/google-session upsert idempotency — bogus session_id returns 401 (graceful, NOT 500); unique index on user_sessions.session_token confirmed present (name+unique flag verified); calling update_one({session_token}, upsert=True) TWICE with the same token does NOT throw DuplicateKeyError and yields exactly 1 row; two independent session tokens for the same user coexist (proves NO delete_many({user_id}) exists before upsert → prior sessions are preserved when the same user re-authenticates via Google). (4) Regressions — signup returns requires_verification=true and lowercase-normalized email (test updated to match), signup w/o password → 422, anonymous returns token+user with auth_provider=anonymous and token authenticates against /auth/me, POST /api/stories with valid feud_id → 200 with hydrated story, quota-exceeded (20 pre-seeded) → 429, invalid feud_id → 404. Test file: /app/backend/tests/test_auth_session_regression.py. Fixture uses seed user chat_a@test.it from /app/memory/test_credentials.md and BASE_URL from EXPO_PUBLIC_BACKEND_URL. Note: the real Emergent OAuth handshake cannot be end-to-end tested from a headless env (needs a live session_id from Emergent's consent screen), so the idempotency invariant is validated at the DB layer against the exact update_one call used in server.py:912.
action_items: No backend action required — auth session flow (JWT + Google session_token) works and is idempotent.

Frontend side (out of scope for this iteration but noted): the two AuthContext.tsx fixes (retry-3x + 401/403-only token wipe; dedup Set + processingLock ref for session_id) are the correct mitigations. Monitor logs for repeated google-session calls with the same session_id — if they persist despite the frontend dedup, consider adding a server-side short-window in-memory cache keyed by session_id to short-circuit duplicate Emergent lookups (currently every duplicate call still hits demobackend.emergentagent.com even if the DB upsert is idempotent).

Consider adding to /api/auth/google-session a fallback path: if Emergent returns 401 for a session_id that ALREADY exists in user_sessions (i.e. the Emergent side expired but our DB still has it valid), we could return the local session unchanged instead of forcing the user back to consent. Low priority — only matters if Emergent's session TTL diverges from ours.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py:912 — the google-session upsert is correct, but note that it never touches `updated_at` — created_at gets overwritten to now_utc() on every upsert. This is harmless behavior but slightly misleading if you later add analytics on session age.

server.py:1318 (logout) — only accepts Bearer token via Authorization header. If AuthContext ever calls logout with the token in a body/query param, it will silently succeed without deleting the row. Consider logging a warning when logout is called without a token header so we can catch a silent regression.
server.py:104-113 (get_current_user session fallback) — the datetime tz-normalization is duplicated across many endpoints; extract into a small helper. Not blocking.

The test surface for the Emergent OAuth branch itself (server.py:859-865) has ZERO coverage because it requires a real Emergent session_id. Consider adding a `TEST_MODE` env flag that lets tests inject a mock httpx response — but only if you plan a lot more work in this area; otherwise the DB-layer idempotency test we ship here is sufficient.
seed_data_creation: Used pre-verified seed user chat_a@test.it. Ephemeral TEST_ prefixed rows created in user_sessions and stories collections are cleaned up in fixture teardowns / try-finally blocks. Ephemeral TEST_regress_*@test.it signup rows land in DB with email_verified=false — harmless and can be cleaned periodically.
context_for_next_testing_agent: test_auth_session_regression.py is a good smoke suite for any auth changes: it covers /auth/me, /auth/logout, google-session upsert idempotency at the DB layer, signup, anonymous, and stories quota. Uses seed user chat_a@test.it (email/password login). The Emergent OAuth handshake itself cannot be tested from headless env — only the DB behavior is exercised. If future work touches /auth/google-session, the invariant to preserve is: `db.user_sessions.update_one({session_token}, {$set:...}, upsert=True)` — never `insert_one` (would DuplicateKeyError) and never `delete_many({user_id})` before the upsert (would kill legitimate parallel sessions). The unique index on session_token is created at startup in server.py:4233.
rca_of_issue: N/A — this iteration validated backend robustness after a frontend-only fix to AuthContext.tsx. The frontend fixes (retry-3x on /auth/me network errors, 401/403-only token wipe, session_id dedup Set + processingLock ref, and mobile loginWithGoogle now routing via processSessionUrl instead of double-calling api.googleSession) address the root cause of the repeated Emergent consent screen. The backend was already using upsert semantics on user_sessions (server.py:912, from a prior job) and this suite confirms the invariant still holds: same session_token upserted twice = 1 row, no DuplicateKeyError; different session_tokens for same user coexist and both authenticate. Combined with the frontend dedup, users should no longer trigger duplicate google-session calls, and even if they do, the backend handles it idempotently.
